title: The Windy Sock Show
learning_objectives: Explain how Sam keeps his promise to Grandma despite the missing socks.
Infer what the puppets will tell Grandma from the windy sheet and Sam's plan.
Explain gust, wraps, pair, and lump using the story.
parent_prompts: Before reading: What could Sam make with two socks in a puppet show?
After page 5: Why might the lump help Sam keep his promise? Use pages 1 and 4.
After reading: How does the windy problem give Sam an idea for his promised show?

pages.text: Sam promised Grandma a sock show. His dry blue socks rest over a sheet on the line.
pages.image_alt: Sam watches Grandma beside a white sheet on the washing line. Two unfastened blue socks bend over the sheet's top fold, with their toes resting against its front; only the sheet has pegs.

pages.text: A gust of wind blows the white sheet sideways. Sam laughs at its big, flapping shape.
pages.image_alt: Sam kneels and smiles as the sheet billows sideways. The same two unfastened blue socks remain draped over its top fold, tilting with the wind.

vocabulary.definition: A short, strong rush of wind.
vocabulary.example: A gust makes the sheet flap.

pages.text: The sheet wraps around the line, catching the socks inside. Sam looks up but cannot see them.
pages.image_alt: Sam looks up with open hands at the sheet now rolled around the line. The socks are hidden inside the roll, whose lower edge has a small localized bulge.

vocabulary.example: The sheet wraps around the line and catches the socks.

pages.text: Sam checks the basket for his missing pair. It is empty, so he looks up at the sheet.
pages.image_alt: Sam kneels at the rim of an empty washing basket beneath the rolled white sheet.

vocabulary.example: Sam looks for his pair of matching blue socks.

pages.text: Grandma feels a lump inside the rolled sheet. Sam hopes his socks are hidden inside that little bump.
pages.image_alt: Grandma touches a small rounded lump protruding below the rolled sheet, distinct from its long folds, while Sam looks up beside her.

vocabulary.example: The hidden socks make a lump in the sheet.

pages.text: Grandma opens the sheet while Sam holds its corner. Two blue socks slide out onto the green grass.

quiz.explanation: Sam promised Grandma a sock show on page 1. He keeps searching on page 4 and puts the socks on his hands on page 7 to give that show.

quiz.prompt: What will Sam's puppets probably talk about?

options.text: Their time inside the windy sheet
Their time inside the washing basket

quiz.explanation: Sam wants the puppets to tell Grandma about their windy ride on page 7. Page 3 tells us what that ride was: the sheet wrapped around the line and caught the socks inside.

quiz.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

options.text: Changing a promise to make washing easier
Giving the promised show despite a problem
Learning a puppet game from Grandma

quiz.explanation: Sam promises Grandma a sock show on page 1. The sheet catches his socks on page 3, but he finds them and Grandma watches the promised show on page 8.

quiz.prompt: Tell how Sam keeps his promise and uses the windy problem in his sock show.
quiz.rubric: not yet: names socks or the sheet without a link; with support: says the socks hide in the sheet and come out with prompting; independent: connects Sam's promise, socks caught in the roll, the empty basket, finding the socks, and his plan to tell their windy ride with the sheet as a curtain
quiz.explanation: A connected retell explains how Sam finds the socks to keep his promise and plans to make their windy ride the puppets' story, with the sheet behind them as a curtain.

activities.prompt: Put Sam's promise, search, and show in order.

items.text: Sam promises Grandma a sock show.
The socks slide out of the sheet.

prompts: Why does Sam keep searching after he finds the basket empty? Use his promise.
How does the windy sheet give Sam something for his puppets to tell Grandma?

off_screen_prompt: Use your hands as two pretend sock puppets. Tell Grandma the socks' windy ride: resting over the sheet, getting caught inside, and sliding out. Explain how Sam keeps his promise.
